audit.why: EVEN fits 50.64% over 393 games. Gnar owns levels 1-2 outright before Spinning Slash and Fury are meaningful; from level 3 on it is a Rage-versus-Fury coinflip; two items is his.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows contradicted their own whys: whys[2] says 'he edges it the moment he Fury-stacks and E-spins' (stored Gnar), whys[4] says 'Level 6 adds no dueling tool for either of you' (stored Gnar), whys[6] says 'he reclaims the 1v1' (stored Gnar).
audit.why: The packet chart (Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Tryndamere) matches the prose in every row. Spikes stay: Gnar level 2, Rage-gated 4-5, an even level 6 because Undying Rage answers the wall-combo, Tryndamere at two items on crit plus sustain.
audit.corrected: win[2]=Skill, win[4]=Skill, win[6]=Tryndamere with matching phases sides, and phases[2], [4], [6] whys rewritten. One atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is never mentioned anywhere on the page, and the early block gives advice that walks straight into it: 'kite back with the Q slow and Hyper move speed'. Mocking Shout reduces AD for everyone nearby but only slows enemies whose BACKS ARE TURNED to him — so a Gnar who turns and runs eats a slow that a Gnar who backs away facing him does not.
audit.why: This is the whole kiting pattern of the matchup and it was absent. It is also the reason Gnar loses chases he should win: the slow is self-inflicted by the retreat animation direction.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout (W, 850 range, 14s) cuts AD in an area and slows only enemies facing away — retreat facing him. Spinning Slash (E, 650 range, 12s at rank 1) is his gap-close. Bloodlust (Q, 12s) consumes Fury to heal, and his AD rises as his health falls, so Grievous Wounds timing decides the extended trade. Undying Rage (R, 120s at rank 1) holds him alive at 1 HP, so bait it before you spend Mega.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Tryndamere must walk into your range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Spinning Slash (650 range, 12s) closes it — level 3 is even, so kite while facing him.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Tryndamere's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Level 6 is even: your wall-combo kills, but Undying Rage holds him at 1 HP for five seconds and he spin-kites the follow-up.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in, crit DPS plus Undying Rage outlasts your form-locked burst — he reclaims the duel, so fight with your team.

edits.before: Mini Gnar owns the opening levels: your ranged autos and Boomerang chip Tryndamere down while his E-spin still can't reach you, and a level-2 Hyper third-hit proc plus a Boomerang is a free chunk and a shove. The lane flips the instant his Fury stacks and he E-spins in — your Mini body is fragile with no hard escape, so kite back with the Q slow and Hyper move speed instead of greeding a fourth auto into his all-in.
edits.after: Mini Gnar owns the opening levels: ranged autos and Boomerang chip Tryndamere down while Spinning Slash still can't reach you, and a level-2 Hyper third-hit proc plus a Boomerang is a free chunk and a shove. The lane flips when his Fury stacks and he spins in. Kite on the Q slow and Hyper move speed — but Mocking Shout (W, 850) only slows targets with their backs turned, so back away facing him and it is AD reduction alone.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Kite it out. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 — bait it, then take the lane.

edits.before: That is Tryndamere's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Bloodlust heals off Fury on 12s, and his AD climbs the lower his health falls.

edits.before: Getting caught at zero rage right after Mega ends — that 15-second window is when Gnars die.
edits.after: Mocking Shout slows only when your back is turned — retreat facing him, 850 range.

notes: Mocking Shout appeared nowhere on this page, and the early block's kiting instruction ('kite back') is exactly what triggers its slow — it only slows enemies whose backs are turned. That is now stated in early, phases[2].why and dontsFull[2].d. Everything else on this page was accurate: no fabricated names, and the Undying Rage / anti-heal framing was already correct, so I added numbers rather than rewriting it.
